blogs.title: Beyond the Signature: Electronic Certifications and the Definition of 'Receipt' in State Statute
blogs.description: An analysis of the Fifth Circuit's statutory interpretation of Louisiana's insurance cancellation law in the face of digital automation. This post examines how the court utilized Black's Law Dictionary to define 'receipt' and 'certification' without explicit legislative guidance, determining that computerized email notifications and corporate certifications satisfy the statute's requirements without individualized signatures.

blogs.title: Preserving the Certification Pipeline: Why the Fifth Circuit Declined to Certify a Louisiana Insurance Question
blogs.description: A procedural examination of the court's decision to reject the plaintiffs' request to have the court certify statutory interpretation questions to the Louisiana Supreme Court. This post analyzes the Fifth Circuit's standard for certification refusal under *Jefferson v. Lead Indus. Ass'n* and what this decision signals for federal courts navigating unclear state laws in the modern judiciary.

blogs.title: Digital Efficiency vs. Legislative Rigor: The 'Strict Adherence' Doctrine in Modernized Auto-Insurance
blogs.description: An exploration of Louisiana's strict adherence doctrine for insurance cancellations and its application to automated contract termination. This post discusses the policy rationale behind the statute (fixing cancellation timestamps and preserving cure periods) and evaluates whether GoAuto's computer-assisted workflow aligns with or undermines the protectionist intent of the original legislative scheme.
